title: Type-II site subspace with persistent Mirror site coordinate
hypothesis: For synthetic sites whose dominant channel subspaces differ by antenna phase ramps, a shared Type-II base subspace plus small persistent site coordinates preserves beamforming rate while reducing total serialized model-plus-feedback description versus storing a separate subspace per site.
scope: Synthetic narrowband 8-antenna channel model; not a PA289 reproduction, measured channel data, or field trial.

storage.authority: actual torch.save decoded persistent inference payload bytes; total description also reports online feedback bits separately

success_gate: In every fresh world, Mirror mean rate is >=95% of full quantized CSI and >=95% of stored per-site Type-II; per-site persistent+online description is <=80% of stored Type-II while pilot probes are counted separately.
failure_gate: Any fresh world misses quality or total description gate, or Mirror exactly aliases the native phase-parametric Type-II control.
boundaries: No multi-user scheduling/interference, coherence-time signaling, RF energy, latency, or public data claim.
Native phase-parametric Type-II is an explicit low-cost control; a win against only stored subspaces is not Mirror-specific evidence.
